meta.tagline: Duolingo won't teach you this — Stockholm edition (what you actually hear).

categories.title: Ordering a beer/food like a local (Sweden)
categories.description: Q → A → what they'll probably say

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: You're at a Swedish bar and the bartender asks what you want.

question.es: Vad får det lov att vara?

answers.en: A large strong beer, please — 50cl, over 5%.

exchanges.notes: The bartender opens with this. "En stor stark" is what most people order — a 50cl beer over 5%, so it is bigger and stronger than a default pint, not a plain one.

situation.en: You've ordered a beer and they ask how you want it.

likelyReply.es: Vilken vill du ha? / Nån särskild?
likelyReply.en: Which one do you want? / Any specific one?

situation.en: The bartender asks whether you want food as well.

question.es: Vill du ha något att äta också?

likelyReply.en: Here you go. / That'll be [AMOUNT] SEK.

situation.en: You've paid and they ask whether you want a receipt.
You want to know what's on draft before you commit to an order.

question.en: What have you got on tap?

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: The bartender wants to see ID before serving you.

exchanges.notes: Sweden IDs hard: 18 to drink in a bar, 20 to buy at Systembolaget. "Leg" is short for legitimation.

situation.en: You walk in with friends and can't tell if you seat yourselves.

question.es: Kan vi sitta var som helst?

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: You're paying and they ask how.

exchanges.notes: Cash is genuinely rare and plenty of Swedish bars refuse it outright. Swish is the local phone-to-phone app and needs a Swedish bank.

items.en: Is Swish okay? (only relevant with friends and some places)
Cheers! — with eye contact, every single time.
The default Swedish order: a large strong lager.
A warmer thank you than a plain tack.
Can we share? — splitting plates is completely normal.
That's everything, thanks — closing an order.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: A colleague or friend suggests coffee in the middle of the afternoon.

question.en: Shall we go for a fika?

exchanges.notes: Fika is coffee, something sweet and sitting down — all three. Declining is fine; proposing a time instead is better.

situation.en: You're at the counter of a café and know what you want.

question.es: En kaffe och en kanelbulle, tack.
question.en: A coffee and a cinnamon bun, please.

answers.en: Would you like it warmed up?

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: Your cup is empty and someone comes round with the pot.

exchanges.notes: Påtår is the free second cup and it really is free. A third one is a tretår.

situation.en: You want to check the refill won't appear on the bill.

answers.en: Yes, as much as you like.

situation.en: The buns behind the glass aren't labelled.

question.es: Vad är det för bullar idag?
question.en: What buns have you got today?

situation.en: They ring you up and need to know whether you're staying.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You're getting up from the table you shared with someone.

exchanges.notes: Said to whoever you sat with, every time. Leaving without it reads as cold.

situation.en: Everything in the counter is sweet and you'd rather have something else.

question.en: Do you have anything without sugar?

categories.title: Starting a convo/basic survival (Stockholm)
categories.description: Q → A → what they'll probably say

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: Someone greets you.

exchanges.notes: "Tja" is the casual Stockholm hello.

situation.en: Someone asks how you're doing.
You need help and want to check whether they speak English.
You didn't catch what someone just said.

likelyReply.es: Jag kan säga det på engelska.
likelyReply.en: I can say it in English.

situation.en: You don't know a word and want to ask what it is.

question.en: How do you say [WORD] in Swedish?

situation.en: You're looking for a place and stop someone to ask.

answers.es: Där borta. / Rakt fram. / Till vänster/höger.
answers.en: Over there. / Straight ahead. / To the left/right.

likelyReply.es: Det är nära. / Det tar typ [ANTAL] minuter.
likelyReply.en: It's close. / It takes about [NUMBER] minutes.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: Someone you've just met is leaving and says you'll be in touch.

exchanges.notes: Usually means nothing will happen. Say it back, mean it as much as they did, and take no offence.

situation.en: You've been talking a while and never got their name.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: Someone who fed you a month ago greets you with this.

answers.en: Thank you too — it was fun!

likelyReply.en: We should do it again soon.

exchanges.notes: Said the next time you meet anyone who hosted you, however long ago. There is no English for it, and not saying it is noticed.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: You've just stepped into someone's flat.

question.es: Du kan ta av dig skorna där.
question.en: You can leave your shoes there.

exchanges.notes: Shoes off indoors, all year, no exceptions and no discussion. Take them off before you're asked.

situation.en: You've been invited to someone's home for the evening.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: You've been standing at a counter and someone points at the machine.

question.en: Have you taken a queue ticket?

exchanges.notes: Ticket queues run everything from the pharmacy to the deli counter. Standing in line without one gets you nowhere at all.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: The bus is filling up and the seat beside someone is the last one.

exchanges.notes: On a half-empty bus Swedes spread out. Sitting beside a stranger while seats are free is the odd move, not the polite one.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: A Swedish friend invites you over on a Friday evening.

answers.en: I'd love to — what shall I bring?

likelyReply.en: Just crisps — we'll do the rest.

exchanges.notes: Friday cosiness: sofa, tacos, television. A real national institution, with its own name and its own crisps.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: You've suggested meeting up and get this back.

exchanges.notes: Swedish for no, most of the time. Ask once more and you'll get a straight answer; ask twice and you won't.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You're pouring someone a drink and want to check the amount.

exchanges.notes: Lagom is the national value: not too much, not too little. Used about a measure, it is a compliment.

note.es: Slang level: medium → heavy. Items marked young are more common among younger people and online.
note.en: If you want to sound local but safe, stick to the ones without a young badge.

phrases.en: Short for bara — "just", often as filler.
To follow / to catch on — slangier than fatta.
Can't be bothered / don't have the energy.
Really good / really fun. Not as strong as the English equivalent.
Really, seriously — an intensifier prefix alongside skit-.
Nice one! — about something done well, not about a person.
Taxi — old Söder slang. You'll hear it; saying it dates you.
Södermalm — the southern island, and a whole personality with it.
The nightlife square — expensive, and fully aware of it.
The transport network — the card, the app and the turnstile.
The pre-party — where most of a Swedish night actually happens.
The pub — "ut på krogen" is going out for the night.
A shot of snaps, usually with a song attached to it.
Systembolaget, the state off-licence. Nobody says the whole word.
3.5% supermarket beer — the only kind sold outside Systembolaget.
Like / sort of — sits next to typ, often in the same sentence.
Yes, actually — contradicts a negative, the way German uses doch.
Hmm, sort of — the Swedish yes-and-no.

subsections.title: The glue — tiny words that carry a conversation

phrases.en: That's right / oh, right — the remembering noise.
Well I never! — surprise, usually delighted.

note.es: Swedish profanity is common in speech, but still context-sensitive.
note.en: Avoid it around kids and in formal settings.

phrases.en: Oh my god — mild, and safe in any company.
Oh bother! — gently ridiculous and completely harmless.
Cut it out! — also "get out of here" in disbelief.
Ugh, hell — extremely common, and stronger than it looks written down.

subsections.title: "I didn't mean it" escape hatch & soft insults

phrases.en: I didn't mean anything by it.
A silly, fussing, faintly ridiculous person.

categories.title: Calling someone attractive (Sweden)
categories.description: Flirt lines that don't land badly

note.es: Only flirt if it feels mutual. Keep it light and accept a no immediately.
note.en: Back off without arguing or guilt-tripping.

phrases.es: Du är lätt att prata med.

phrases.en: I like the way you think.

phrases.es: Jag tycker du är riktigt snygg.
Ska vi ta en öl nån gång?
phrases.en: Want to grab a beer sometime?
Are you staying a bit longer?
Maybe we should see each other again?

phrases.es: Det var kul att prata med dig.
phrases.en: It was good talking to you.

phrases.es: Ingen press om du inte vill.
phrases.en: No pressure if you don't want to.

phrases.es: Säg bara till om du inte är bekväm.
phrases.en: Just say if you're not comfortable.

phrases.es: Är det okej om jag säger en grej?
phrases.en: Is it okay if I say something?

phrases.es: Är det okej om jag bjuder dig på en drink?
phrases.en: Is it okay if I buy you a drink?
Do you want me to go?

phrases.es: Säg till om det blir för mycket.
phrases.en: Say if it gets to be too much.
Would you rather be left alone?
Does this feel all right to you?

categories.title: Getting around (taxi + metro) — Stockholm
categories.description: Q → A → what they'll probably say

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You've landed and you're looking for where the taxis are.

question.en: Excuse me, where are the taxis?

exchanges.notes: Arlanda Express runs from the same arrivals hall — swap taxi for tåget.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Before getting in, you want to know what a taxi into town costs.

question.en: What does it cost to the centre?

exchanges.notes: Swedish taxis set their own prices — the comparison price is posted on the window, and asking first is normal.

situation.en: You've landed at Arlanda and want the fast train rather than a taxi.
The express train costs more than you want to pay.

question.es: Går det någon buss till stan?
question.en: Is there a bus into town?

answers.en: The airport coaches, just outside the terminal.

situation.en: The officer at passport control wants your documents.
You need to find the baggage belts.
You want a travel card before you get into the city.

question.en: Where can I buy an SL card?

answers.en: At the machine by the exit.

situation.en: Your roaming isn't working and you need to message someone.
You get into a taxi and the driver asks where to.
You've arrived and want the driver to pull over.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You're about to get in and want the price settled first.

exchanges.notes: Swedish taxis set their own fares and the unbooked ones at ranks can be eye-watering. Agree a fast pris, or check the yellow price sticker on the window.

situation.en: You've got no cash and want to check before setting off.
You're at the car with a suitcase and the boot is shut.
You're cutting it fine for a train and want to know the journey time.
You need the fare receipted for work.
The driver reads the address back before pulling away.
You're on the street looking for the metro.

question.es: Var är tuben? / Var är Tunnelbanan?

situation.en: You know your destination but not which line to take.
You want to know whether the line takes you there directly.
You're on board and don't know how far your stop is.
It's past midnight and you don't know if the metro is still going.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: An inspector in plain clothes asks for your ticket mid-journey.

exchanges.notes: Inspectors board without warning and the fine is 1 500 kronor. Tap in even for one stop.

situation.en: Two platforms serve the same line and you don't know which you want.
You're on a platform and want someone to confirm you're on the right side.
You've come out of the wrong exit and nothing looks familiar.

answers.en: Where are you trying to get to?

situation.en: Someone has pointed the way and you want to know if it's walkable.
You're at a stop with four bus numbers on the sign.

question.en: Which bus goes to the centre?

answers.en: The number four, from the other side.

situation.en: Directions in Swedish are going too fast for you.

question.en: Can you show me on the map?

answers.es: Vi är här, du ska dit.
answers.en: We're here — you want to be there.

situation.en: The metro has stopped for the night and you're still out.

question.en: Does the night bus go from here?

situation.en: You've been staring at your phone on a corner and someone stops.

answers.en: Yes, please — I can't find it.

likelyReply.en: I'll walk with you part of the way.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You've lost your bearings completely and need any landmark at all.

exchanges.notes: Stockholm is fourteen islands. Finding the water usually tells you which one you're standing on.

situation.en: You want the old town and don't know which line serves it.

question.es: Hur kommer jag till Gamla stan?
question.en: How do I get to Gamla stan?

categories.title: At a restaurant (Sweden)
categories.description: Q → A → what they'll probably say

situation.en: You arrive at a restaurant with one other person.
You've finished eating and want to pay.

question.en: Can we get the bill, please?

likelyReply.es: Vill ni betala tillsammans eller separat?
likelyReply.en: Do you want to pay together or separately?

situation.en: The waiter asks whether you want water.
The server comes over once you've had a look at the menu.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: It's lunchtime and you'd rather be told what's good than read the menu.

answers.en: The dish of the day is good.

exchanges.notes: Dagens is the weekday lunch deal — a main, salad, bread and coffee for one fixed price. It is always the best value on the menu.

situation.en: You've decided on the lunch deal.

question.en: I'll have the dish of the day, please.

situation.en: You need to flag a food allergy before you order.
They clear your plate and ask how it was.
A plate arrives that nobody at your table asked for.

question.es: Ursäkta, jag beställde inte det här.
question.en: Excuse me, I didn't order this.

situation.en: Your food has been sitting under a lamp too long.
The bread basket emptied faster than you expected.

question.es: Kan vi få lite mer bröd?
question.en: Could we have a bit more bread?

situation.en: Everyone else has been served and you haven't.

question.en: We're still waiting for our food.

situation.en: You've finished your drink and want the same again.
You need the toilet and can't see a sign.

answers.en: Right at the back on the left.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: You're a group of four and the server picks up the card machine.

exchanges.notes: Splitting is completely normal in Sweden and the machine will do it item by item if you ask.

situation.en: You're leaving and want to say the meal was good.

question.en: That was really good, thank you.

categories.title: Checking in (hotel/hostel/Airbnb) (Sweden)
categories.description: Q → A → what they'll probably say

situation.en: You arrive at the desk and need to claim your booking.
They have your booking up and confirm the length of stay.
You want to know whether breakfast is part of the rate.
You're planning the last morning of the trip.

question.en: When do we have to check out?

situation.en: Your flight is tonight but the room goes at eleven.

question.en: Can we leave our bags here?

situation.en: You're in the room and want to get online.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You've heard Swedish hotels usually have one and want to use it.

exchanges.notes: Most Swedish hotels have one. Ask about towel and swimwear rules before you go down — they vary and nobody will warn you.

situation.en: You hand the key back on your way out.

likelyReply.es: Tack för att ni sa till.

categories.title: Shops, cashless Sweden & Systembolaget
categories.description: Q → A → what they'll probably say

situation.en: You've been browsing a minute and an assistant approaches.

question.es: Kan jag hjälpa dig med något?
question.en: Can I help you with anything?

likelyReply.en: Just say if you're wondering about anything.

situation.en: The only one left on the rail is too small.

question.es: Har ni den i större storlek?
question.en: Do you have this in a bigger size?

situation.en: You want to try something on before committing.

answers.en: The fitting rooms are over there.

situation.en: There's no price on the thing you're holding.
Yesterday's purchase doesn't fit and you've kept the receipt.
You're at the till with more than you can carry.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You've got notes in your pocket and want to know if they're any use.

exchanges.notes: Sweden is as close to cashless as anywhere. Plenty of shops, cafés and every city bus have not handled a note in years.

situation.en: It's late afternoon and you may need to come back.

subsections.title: Systembolaget — the one shop that matters

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You want wine for dinner and the supermarket had nothing but weak beer.

exchanges.notes: The only place in the country selling anything above 3.5%. Nowhere else, at any price, at any hour.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: You put a bottle on the counter and they look up at you.

exchanges.notes: The limit here is 20, not the 18 that gets you served in a bar, and they ask anyone who looks under 25.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: It's Saturday lunchtime and you're planning the evening.

question.en: Do you close early on Saturdays?

exchanges.notes: This catches out every visitor exactly once. Shut all day Sunday, and the shutters come down at 15:00 on Saturday.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: The wall of bottles means nothing to you and staff are paid to advise.

exchanges.notes: Systembolaget staff are not on commission and will give you a straight answer. Ask them.

situation.en: You've seen two words for beer and don't know what separates them.

question.es: Vad är skillnaden på folköl och starköl?
question.en: What's the difference between folköl and starköl?

answers.es: Folköl är 3,5 — resten finns bara här.
answers.en: Folköl is 3.5 — everything else is only sold here.

situation.en: You want to take something home that you can't get anywhere else.
They don't stock what you're after and you wonder if they can get it.

question.en: Do I have to order in advance?

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: It's a warm evening and everyone in the park seems to have a can.

question.es: Får man dricka öl i parken?
question.en: Are you allowed to drink beer in the park?

answers.es: Officiellt nej, men ingen bryr sig.

exchanges.notes: Banned in most municipalities and quietly tolerated in parks all summer. Keep it calm and tidy and nothing happens.

categories.title: Nightlife — the door, the club, the people (Sweden)
categories.description: Q → A → what they'll probably say

situation.en: You reach the front of the queue and the doorman counts your group.

question.en: How many of you are there?

likelyReply.en: You'll have to wait a bit.

situation.en: The doorman holds a hand out without saying much.
You're at the front and want to know the damage.

question.en: How much is it to get in?

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: It's minus five outside and you're wearing a serious coat.

exchanges.notes: Coat check is close to compulsory in a Swedish winter, and they will not let you carry a big coat inside.

situation.en: A friend said they'd put your name down.

answers.en: No — can we get in anyway?

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Someone in your group is nineteen and you want to check before queueing.

exchanges.notes: Clubs set their own limit and it is often 20, 23 or higher — well above the legal 18. It is usually on the door.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: The doorman looks past you and shakes his head.

exchanges.notes: Arguing with a Swedish doorman is the one reliable way to make the refusal permanent.

situation.en: You can hear something through the door and want to know what you're walking into.
You've started talking to a group at the bar.
This bar has emptied out and you'd rather not end the night here.
Someone notices you're standing on your own.

question.en: Are you here on your own?

likelyReply.en: Come and hang out with us.

situation.en: The group you've joined is putting coats on.

question.en: Where are you off to after this?

situation.en: Someone offers to get the next one in.

question.es: Vill du ha något att dricka?
question.en: Do you want something to drink?

situation.en: You've got locals in front of you and want a better bar than this one.

question.es: Har ni något bra ställe att rekommendera?
question.en: Do you know anywhere good to recommend?

answers.en: Try the place round the corner.

situation.en: You're done for the night and want to leave without a fuss.
You're all leaving at once and a taxi is cheaper shared.

answers.es: Ja, vi bor åt samma håll.
answers.en: Yes — we're going the same way.

phrases.en: A pub crawl — literally a round of the bars.
The doorman — and the person who decides how your night goes.
To move on to the next place.
The late-night sandwich you eat on the way home.
An unlicensed after-hours club — literally a "black club".
To hang out — the default word for doing nothing much together.

categories.title: How drunk are you? (Sweden)
categories.description: The whole ladder, and the moments where you have to pick a rung out loud.

note.en: Sweden grades this finely and talks about it plainly. The one to learn first is full — it means drunk, never "full" as in fed.

phrases.en: Intoxicated — the formal word, the one on the signs.
Drunk. Never "full" as in fed — that is mätt.

situation.en: A few drinks in, someone checks how you're getting on.
Someone is working out whether to put you down for another round.
You stand up and the room moves more than it should.
Someone arrives at the table with shots for the whole group.

answers.es: Nej, jag är rätt packad redan.

situation.en: You've found your limit and want to stop at it.
A stranger has noticed the state your friend is in.

answers.es: Hon är asfull, jag tar hem henne.
answers.en: She's hammered — I'm taking her home.

likelyReply.en: Do you two need a taxi?

situation.en: It's the next day and you're owning up to how it went.

question.en: I was completely blackout last night.

situation.en: You're leaving and someone wants to know you'll make it back.

question.en: Can you get home all right?

situation.en: The round is going in and you'd rather skip this one.
It's your round and you want something soft without a discussion.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You drove out to the summer house and want that understood early.

question.es: Jag kör, så jag dricker inget.
question.en: I'm driving, so I'm not drinking.

exchanges.notes: Sweden's limit is 0.2 — effectively nothing at all. Saying you're driving ends the conversation on the spot.

situation.en: Someone won't take your first no about one more.
You've drunk more than you've eaten and you can feel it.
You've decided the night is over for you.

answers.en: Shall I come outside with you?

situation.en: A friend is pacing you and pushes a glass across.

question.en: Have a glass of water in between.

situation.en: You're outside the bar and in no state to work out a night bus.

question.es: Kan du beställa en taxi åt mig?
question.en: Could you order me a taxi?

categories.title: The morning after & the pharmacy (Sweden)
categories.description: Q → A → what they'll probably say

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Your head is splitting and you need something for it.

question.en: Do you have anything for a headache?

exchanges.notes: Ipren and Alvedon are the brand names Swedes actually say, the way Britons say Nurofen.

situation.en: The pharmacist looks at you and asks what's wrong.
You want to know whether you need a doctor first.
You're badly dehydrated and water alone isn't touching it.
You've got the box and don't want to overdo it.

question.es: Hur ofta ska jag ta det?
question.en: How often should I take it?

answers.en: Three times a day at most.

situation.en: You need a pharmacy and don't know the area.
Before handing anything over they check what else you take.

question.en: Are you on any other medication?

situation.en: A long Nordic summer day has caught you out.

question.es: Jag har bränt mig i solen.

phrases.en: The specific dread about what you said last night. Sweden names it; almost nobody else does.
The day after — used on its own as a noun.
Hair of the dog — literally "a restorer".
A crushing hangover — literally a "concrete cap".
Never again. Said monthly, meant every time.

categories.title: Robbed, lost & emergencies (Sweden)
categories.description: Q → A → what they'll probably say

situation.en: You reach for your wallet on the tunnelbana and it's gone.
You need to report it and don't know where to go.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Your insurer won't pay out without a crime number.

question.en: I'd like to file a report.

exchanges.notes: Your insurer will want the anmälan number. You can also file it by phone on 114 14 rather than queueing.

situation.en: Your passport is gone and you fly tomorrow.
You've come out of a club alone and your group has vanished.
Someone in your group is hurt and needs seeing to.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: A stranger has stopped to help and is reaching for their phone.

exchanges.notes: 112 works anywhere in Sweden, free, from any phone. For anything short of an emergency, 1177 is the medical advice line.

situation.en: Your phone has died and everything you need is on it.

categories.title: For the girls (Sweden)
categories.description: What it sounds like, and how to end it.

note.en: Say these at normal volume or louder. Sweden will not think you are overreacting, and staff have a legal duty to step in.

subsections.title: What it sounds like & shutting it down

situation.en: A man you don't know steps into your path outside a bar.

question.en: Hey gorgeous, are you on your own?

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: Someone tells you to smile as you walk past.

exchanges.notes: The comeback is the tell: anyone who calls you sur for declining was never being friendly.

situation.en: Someone has been talking at you for ten minutes and won't take a hint.

question.en: I want to be left alone.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: A stranger puts a hand on you in a crowded bar.

exchanges.notes: Say it loudly. The volume is the point — it turns heads, and that is what makes it stop.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: A man insists on buying you a drink you didn't ask for.

question.es: Jag bjuder dig på en drink.
question.en: Let me get you a drink.

answers.es: Nej tack, jag har redan en.
answers.en: No thanks — I've already got one.

exchanges.notes: Never take a drink you didn't watch being poured, however well it is meant.

situation.en: Polite has stopped working and you're finished being polite.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You get the bartender's attention about the man who won't leave.

exchanges.notes: Say it to the staff rather than only to your friends. Swedish venues have a duty to act, and generally do.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You want the fastest exit line, whether or not it's true.

question.es: Jag är här med min kille.

exchanges.notes: It shouldn't work better than no. It often does. Use whatever ends it fastest.

situation.en: You want someone with you between the door and the taxi.

question.es: Kan du följa med mig till taxin?
question.en: Can you walk me to the taxi?

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Nothing has happened yet but you want to leave anyway.

question.es: Jag känner mig inte trygg här.

exchanges.notes: You never have to justify this. Trygg — safe, secure — is a word Swedes take entirely seriously.

situation.en: You don't want to be on your own for the next few minutes.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Two sips in, your drink has hit you far harder than it should have.

question.es: Jag tror någon har lagt något i mitt glas.
question.en: I think someone put something in my drink.

exchanges.notes: Tell the staff, not only your friends. Swedish clubs have a procedure for this and will use it.

situation.en: A bartender has clocked that something is wrong.
You're leaving alone and want someone to know you got back.

question.es: Jag hör av mig när jag är hemma.

situation.en: He's waiting outside and you'd rather not walk out yet.

question.es: Kan jag vänta här tills han går?
question.en: Can I wait here until he leaves?

situation.en: Your group is drifting towards the door and you don't want to be last.
